newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trial of ex-Vichy official set to start October 6.
newsitem.headline: Trial of ex-Vichy official set to start October 6.

text.p: The trial of former French cabinet minister Maurice Papon, who is accused of ordering the deportation of 1,560 Jews to Nazi death camps during World War Two, will open on October 6, justice sources said on Monday.

After 15 years of legal wrangling, France's Supreme Court in January ordered Papon, who was secretary-general of the southwestern Bordeaux region in 1942-1944, to face a jury for crimes against humanity.
The trial is expected to last between two and three months.
The trial date was set for after the summer holidays to allow time to arrange the courtroom for the hundreds of people -- witnesses, victims' families and press members -- expected to attend.
Papon, now 86, enjoyed an illustrious post-war career until his war-time record became known, serving as Paris police chief in 1958-1967 and budget minister in the 1970s.
He denies any wrongdoing and says he used his position to help the Resistance.
